findings.location: PDF/printed p. 3, Theorem 1.2; pp. 24–25, Corollary 5.5(a). Compare p. 23, Corollary 5.4(a), and p. 22, Assumption 5.1.
findings.claim: Uniform-weight divergence in Theorem 1.2 and unconditioned Markov-mass divergence in Corollary 5.5(a) do not imply divergence of the actual denominator m(tau appended x0).
findings.admissible_example: Use F2 with alphabet (a,b,A=a^-1,B=b^-1), pi=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4), and P=(I+C)/2 for the directed cycle a→b→A→B→a. P is doubly stochastic, stationary with pi, has zero inverse transitions, and P^3 is strictly positive. The stationary Markov shift is nonatomic and mixing. Let f=1_{x0=a} and let tau_n be the root plus all reduced words of positive length at most n ending in b. These are finite left-Cayley subtrees and exclude A.
findings.decisive_evidence: Each positive level ending in b has uniform mass and Markov mass 1/4. Thus mu(tau_n)=m(tau_n)=1+n/4 tends to infinity. Since P(b,a)=0, m(tau_n appended a)=1/4 and the average is f(x)=1 for every n on {x0=a}, a set of measure 1/4. Boundary-invariant sets are shift-invariant; shift ergodicity gives conditional expectation 1/4. Exact enumeration through height 8 agrees with the analytic proof for all n.
findings.proof_or_calculation: English report Section 2 and independently executed counterexample_check.py, using exact Fraction and SymPy arithmetic.
findings.repair_boundary: Require m(tau appended x0)→infinity, as in Corollary 5.4(a). For a finite alphabet, positivity of every permitted transition also makes m(tau) a sufficient mass condition, but does not identify a general m with mu. The paper defines uniform mu only for finite rank. No nonsingularity of the full boundary action is claimed for this example; that is not an additional stated hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 or Corollary 5.5.
findings.impact: This directly falsifies a principal boundary convergence conclusion. It does not refute the backward Theorem 4.7 or the uniform pmp Theorem 1.1, and is not claimed to meet the extra boundary weak-mixing assumption of Theorem 6.2.

independent_verification.conditions: The printed boundary statements assume stationary Markov weights with positive initial distribution and zero inverse transitions, and finite left-Cayley trees excluding x(0)^-1; they do not add nonsingularity of the full boundary action or positivity of every permitted transition. The counterexample uses r=2, bounded f, and a stationary, primitive, nonatomic chain. It does not claim the additional boundary weak-mixing hypothesis of Theorem6.2.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Order the alphabet (a,b,A,B), A=a^-1 and B=b^-1. Let C be the directed cycle a->b->A->B->a, P=(I+C)/2 and pi=(1/4,...,1/4). All row/column sums are1, inverse entries vanish, and P^3=(I+3C+3C^2+C^3)/8 has all entries positive. The eigenvalues of P are1,(1+i)/2,0,(1-i)/2, so P^n tends to the uniform projection; Markov cylinder mixing extends to the stationary shift, hence ergodicity. Every admissible length-k cylinder has mass1/(4*2^(k-1)), implying nonatomicity; periodic trajectories are a null countable set. For f=1_[a], every exactly beta-invariant Borel set is shift invariant because sigma(x)=x(0)^-1.x; hence bar f=1/4 a.e. Set tau_n={identity} union all reduced words of lengths1..n ending in b. Removing the first letter preserves this set until the root, so it is a finite left-Cayley tree and excludes A. At level k there are3^(k-1) words ending in b, so its uniform mass is1/4; stationarity also gives total Markov mass pi(b)=1/4. Both m_u(tau_n) and m(tau_n) equal1+n/4. On [a], which has measure1/4, P(b,a)=0 makes m(w appended a)=0 for every nonempty w in tau_n, while the root contributes m(a)=1/4. There is no cancellation; the denominator stays1/4 and every average equals f(x)=1, contradicting the target1/4 for every n. This is an all-height analytic counterexample, not an extrapolation from finite code.
independent_verification.impact: The translation of the correct appended-mass growth condition in Corollary5.4 to Theorem1.2 and Corollary5.5(a) is false for their stated class. This is a failed principal advertised consequence and remains Major even though the local corrected condition is easy to write.
independent_verification.repair_boundary: Require m(tau appended x(0))->infinity as already in Corollary5.4. For a fixed finite alphabet and all permitted transitions positive, c_i=min_{j!=i^-1}P(j,i)>0 gives m(tau appended i)>=pi(i)+c_i(m(tau)-1); this repairs the unconditioned m-mass implication. It does not in general compare an arbitrary m to m_u, and infinitely many generators do not provide a uniform positive minimum. The m_u notation is itself only defined here for finite rank. No counterexample to Theorem1.3/4.7, uniform pmp Theorem1.1, or Theorem6.2 under its additional intended weak-mixing hypothesis is established. The full boundary action of this counterexample is not asserted to be nonsingular; importing that unstated restriction would change the theorem being judged.

findings.location: p. 20, last line of the proof of Corollary 4.15; p. 26, definition of weak mixing; p. 25, uniform example.
findings.claim: The c-fat norm bound should be c^(-1/p); the product condition should say ergodic; uniform irreducibility requires r>=2.
findings.decisive_evidence: A complete averaging operator fixes 1 and is also 1/2-fat, so its norm is at least 1, contradicting the printed bound 1/2. A two-point ergodic flip is a factor of its product with any action; taking a second flip gives a nonconstant invariant sign product, preventing weak mixing. At rank 1 the uniform nonbacktracking matrix is the two-state identity.
findings.repair_boundary: Correct the constants and wording. Uniform boundedness for Lp convergence and the ergodicity used in Lemma 6.7 remain available. No additional principal conclusion is refuted.

independent_verification.conditions: Finite p>=1 for the fat-tree estimate; the weak-mixing quantifier ranges over every ergodic pmp action; the uniform chain is examined also at r=1.
independent_verification.independent_proof: In Corollary3.9 substitute w=c(n+1): the bound is c^(-1/p), not c; for p=infinity it is1. A complete-tree average fixes constants and is also1/2-fat, so its operator norm is at least1 and cannot be<=1/2. Uniform boundedness survives with the corrected constant, and the bounded-function approximation is repaired by choosing its error relative to this constant. For a free group choose an ergodic two-point flip pmp action via its Z/2 quotient. It is a factor of beta times that action; multiplying by another flip leaves the nonconstant sign product invariant. Thus the first product cannot be weakly mixing. The standard property, directly confirmed in GW Definition0.1(5), is that beta times any ergodic pmp action is ergodic, precisely what Lemma6.7 uses. Finally, at r=1 the two-state uniform nonbacktracking P is I_2, hence not irreducible; the claimed irreducibility needs r>=2.
independent_verification.impact: Each identified defect has a specific local correction that preserves the associated intended argument. Main Theorems1.1 and6.2 already impose r>=2. The classification does not rely merely on an inability to refute the final conclusions.
independent_verification.repair_boundary: Replace c by c^(-1/p), adjust approximation constants, replace product-weakly-mixing by product-ergodic in the definition, and state r>=2 for the irreducibility assertion. The external nonsingular weak-mixing and decomposition theorems remain imported and are not fully reproved here.

independent_analytic_reasoning: Null-preserving restriction: the involution exhaustion in Lemma2.2 removes null images of successively chosen positive sets; the chosen B_n are disjoint, so their masses tend to0. The quantitative supremum choice then forces the remaining bad set to be null. Proposition2.4 obtains forward/backward conull invariance and surjectivity. This does not retroactively impose full-boundary nonsingularity in Theorem1.2.

In the aperiodic setting, level masses equal1 and distinct levels do not overlap. Jensen plus the local-global identity yields Corollary3.9. The tiling argument controls the bad-height set of measure<epsilon^2/2 and its backward-weight average via Markov's inequality. The correct retained fraction is (N-L+1)/(N+1)>1-epsilon/2 when L/N<epsilon/2. This fixes the displayed off-by-one without changing the argument.

Greedy tiles are disjoint: if a new root outside an earlier tile had a descendant in it, suffix closure of the earlier tile would force the new root into that tile. Finite height bounds the number of root-depth stages, even when branching is countably infinite.

Adding T(x) to a heavy tree changes its average by a term bounded by (|S|+|f(Tx)|) times a fixed cocycle weight divided by the growing mass. Thus f* is nondecreasing along T; recurrence applied to rational superlevel sets gives a.e. invariance. Finite witnesses are justified by absolute summability on each complete finite-height tree.

For Theorem4.7, after replacing f by f-bar f, take g=min(f*/2,1)>0 and c=int g. Choose finite positive f-g tiles. Truncating only the negative tail Y={f>-M} preserves positive tile integrals. Combining tiling, the local-global bridge and small exceptional-set integrals yields the stated contradiction. For the maximal theorem, choose a minimal finite witness after finite approximation; each rooted descendant subtree must have average>lambda, else removing it improves the remaining witness. These checks do not amount to certifying all imported descriptive-set-theoretic results.

The Gauss branch weight (1+x)/((x+j)(x+j+1)) telescopes: its partial sum through N is1-(1+x)/(x+N+1), tending to1. The standard conull irrational domain and positive continued-fraction digits are required.

For Section6, measure preservation of T(x,y)=(y(0)^-1.x,sigma y) follows from pmp alpha and pi P=pi. Orbit equivalence/cocycle calculations and Lemma6.8 are read with their conull positive-transition restriction. The key identity sum_i m(w appended i)=m(w) is exact including zero transitions and the empty word; it combines all initial letters, unlike F1's single-letter conditioning.

Fubini provides a good y_i in each positive-measure initial-letter cylinder. Finite rank permits a common M controlling all maximal averages and thresholds. For a component with rho-mass<M and m(tau)>2M^2/epsilon, its error is<pi(i)epsilon; for a heavy component use convergence and coefficient<=1. Summing pi(i)=1 gives the stated final error. The uniform-boundary weak-mixing theorem and general ergodic decomposition are external inputs, not newly proved here.
